findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In step 2 (and the ADR 0052 §2 note), say that every agentic re-review runs the agent afresh, with or without code drift, because idempotent reuse is also pipeline-only. List idempotent reuse among the mechanisms that uphold the contract.
evidence: Plan step 2: "upheld by the drift floor, cross-checks and drift refresh ... An agentic re-review after code drift runs the agent afresh and can surface new blocking findings."
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:544 `if engine == "pipeline" and sign and not force and not retry: reused = reuse.idempotent_reuse(...)`
ADR 0052 §2: "Re-running `review-plan` on an unchanged, previously-signed plan — even at a drifted HEAD — MUST yield ... no NEW blocking findings"
findings.finding: The plan understates how far ADR 0052 §2's re-review stability is lost under agentic. ADR 0052 §2 covers re-reviewing an unchanged, signed plan 'even at a drifted HEAD', which includes a re-review at an unchanged HEAD. In the pipeline, that case is handled by `reuse.idempotent_reuse`, which returns the still-valid attestation without re-running the review. That shortcut is pipeline-only too, so an agentic re-review of an unchanged plan at an unchanged HEAD also runs the agent afresh and can surface new blockers. The consequence the plan writes says only 'after code drift'.
scenarios: An operator re-runs `review-plan --engine agentic` on an already-signed, unchanged plan with no code change, expecting the documented reuse. Instead the agent runs again, which is billable, and its non-deterministic output can flip PASS to BLOCK.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the step-2 consequence to: "...is upheld by idempotent reuse, the drift floor, the cross-checks and drift refresh, so it holds for the pipeline engine only. Every agentic re-review, at an unchanged or a drifted HEAD, runs the agent afresh and can surface new blocking findings."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rewrite step 1's first reason so it states the real basis for keeping the drift floor and cross-checks pipeline-only (tuned to pipeline findings and/or operator choice), rather than claiming they would override the blocker-only severity decision.
evidence: 'The drift floor and cross-checks remove findings from the blocking list, so running them on agentic verdicts would override that decision'

Decision section: drift floor drops 'a novel finding ... when its citations miss the drifted files'; cross-checks 'drop contradicted or already-resolved findings'. Neither criterion concerns severity.
findings.finding: The first reason the ADR will record does not support the decision. The 2026-11-09 decision (§3) governs which severities block an agentic verdict: only `blocker`. The drift floor and cross-checks instead drop specific findings for other reasons: citations miss the drifted files, the finding is contradicted, or it is already resolved. Dropping such a finding would not change which severities block, so running these steps would not 'override that decision'. Future readers would inherit a justification that does not hold. The real tradeoff is that these steps are tuned to pipeline findings, as the second reason already says for the floors. It may also be that the operator chose not to apply them.
findings.location: Plan step 1, first sub-bullet ('the operator decided on 2026-11-09 (§3) ... would override that decision')
scenarios: A maintainer later weighs extending the drift floor to agentic reviews to restore ADR 0052 convergence. The ADR tells them doing so conflicts with the blocker-only decision, but it does not, so the recorded rationale steers them wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the first reason with: the drift floor's novelty test and the cross-checks' contradiction and comment-trail checks are calibrated against pipeline findings and prior pipeline attestations. Applying them to agentic findings is untested, so they stay pipeline-only by operator direction (2026-11-13). Applying them would only drop agentic blockers, never add any.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the ADR 0123 §6 rationale, add the concrete mechanical reason: agentic findings carry no `citations`, so `drift_floor` would drop every novel agentic finding. Keep the §3 argument as secondary, or drop it.
evidence: Plan: "The drift floor and cross-checks remove findings from the blocking list, so running them on agentic verdicts would override that decision"
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/agentic_verdict.py map_finding returns keys finding/criteria/evidence/suggested_fix/severity/decision/tier/agentic_id, with no `citations`
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/drift_floor.py:195 reads `finding.get("citations")` with kind == "file" to decide whether a novel finding cites a drifted file
ADR 0123 §3 governs the decision mapping ("Severity alone decides"), not whether findings are pruned later
findings.finding: The main reason the plan gives for keeping the drift floor and cross-checks off under agentic is weak, and it omits the concrete reason in the code. ADR 0123 §3 decides how severity maps to a block/advisory decision. It does not say whether findings can be pruned afterwards. The pipeline also partitions findings by decision and still prunes them in the tail. So 'removing findings from the blocking list would override that decision' does not follow. The concrete reason is this: `agentic_verdict.map_finding` emits only free-text `evidence` and no `citations`, while `drift_floor` drops a novel finding whose `citations` (kind=file) miss the drifted files. Run on an agentic verdict, the drift floor would therefore drop every novel agentic finding, blockers included.
findings.location: Plan step 1, first sub-bullet (rationale for drift floor and cross-checks)
scenarios: A later maintainer reads the ADR, argues that pruning does not conflict with §3, and turns the drift floor on for agentic. Every novel agentic blocker on a code-drifted re-review is then silently dropped and the plan PASSes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the step-1 rationale: "Agentic findings (agentic_verdict.map_finding) carry free-text `evidence` but no `citations`. The drift floor keeps a novel finding only when its file citations hit the drifted files, so on an agentic verdict it would drop every novel finding, blockers included."

The ADR will say that the post-dispatch tail and the 3 pre-dispatch shortcuts (`reuse.idempotent_reuse`, `reuse.verdict_reuse`, `orchestrator.drift_refresh`) are pipeline-only, yet the named test only patches `_apply_review_floors`.
